newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Cuba says economic recovery to continue in 1997.
newsitem.headline: Cuba says economic recovery to continue in 1997.

text.p: Cuba expects its economic recovery to continue in 1997 and wants its Latin American neighbours to help by investing in key sectors, Foreign Affairs Minister Roberto Robaina Gonzalez said Tuesday.
Cuban gross domestic product, which expanded 7.9 percent in 1996, should grow at a slightly faster rate this year, perhaps by eight or nine percent, Gonzalez told reporters in the Brazilian capital.

However, those numbers principally reflected Cuba's economic slump in previous years which was caused by the U.S. blockade of the island and the collapse of the Soviet Union, its main benefactor, he said.
"We are a long way from solving the problems we face," Gonzalez said after presenting Brazilian officials with a list of business opportunities in Cuba.
Areas of specific interest to Brazilian companies included telecommunications and oil. "Cuba is not just a country in need, but one with plenty to offer as well," Gonzalez said.
